_howto: Each tab has a list of terms. Fields: term, def, icon (optional emoji), see (optional page link), phins (true = Phins team term, gets the dolphin badge).

terms.def: A player with the ball is held by an opponent and brought to ground.
The player who makes the tackle / the player with the ball who gets tackled. Both have jobs after the tackle.
When you're tackled and on the ground. You must place or release the ball right away.
Tackled player puts the ball back toward their own team so teammates can secure it.
Tackler must let go of the tackled player right away. Tackled player must let go of the ball.
After a tackle, get out of the way. Players lying around the ball give away penalties.
Ball is on the ground and at least one player from each team is on their feet, over the ball, in contact. No hands allowed.
General term for everything that happens at the tackle and ruck.
A player on their feet grabbing the ball at the tackle before a ruck forms. Legal only before the ruck forms.
Driving opponents away from the ball at the ruck.
The defending team drives over the ball to win it back.
Diving or falling over the ball to protect it. Illegal. Stay on your feet.
The back foot of the last player in the ruck. It sets the offside line.
You must join a ruck or tackle from directly behind it, "through the gate," not from the side.
Ref telling the 9 to play the ball now.
Ball has left the ruck, so the ruck is over and defenders can go.
Everything that isn't a set piece. The ball is live and moving.
Each new attack after a ruck. Phase 1, phase 2, and so on.
A group of 3 forwards who work together to carry, support, and ruck. We have pods of 3: point, support, lazy.
The first person in the pod to get the ball. The carrier.
The main supporter of the point. In charge of getting to the ruck first or accepting a pop pass.

The third person in a pod, standing a few feet behind the scrum half. You still get to the ruck and support. It's called "lazy" because it usually takes the least running to get there from the last breakdown and to the ruck you need to join.
Our forward shape across the field. A flanker on each edge (the 1s), and the tight five plus the 8 in two center pods of 3 (the 3s).
[HANNAH TO PROVIDE: Phins definition of "the channel" and why we stay out of it]
Running with the ball into contact.
Getting past the gain line so the next ruck is fast and easy.
Ball that takes a long time to come out of the ruck. Gives the defense time to set.
Imaginary line across the field where the last breakdown was. Getting past it = going forward.
Picking the ball up from the base of a ruck and charging straight forward.
A hard, straight carry aimed at the defense to suck in tacklers.
A short, soft pass to a teammate right next to you, usually in contact.
Passing the ball while being tackled.
Pretending to pass to fool the defense.
A player running close to the carrier, ready for a pass or to protect the ball.
A teammate binding onto the carrier to drive them forward.
The short side of the field from a breakdown / the wide side.
The imaginary line you must be behind to be in the game. At a ruck it's the hindmost foot.
You're behind the offside line and allowed to play.
How fast the defensive line moves up.
Defense that moves sideways to push attackers toward the touchline.
Defense that sprints up fast to shut attackers down early.
Running around behind a ruck to get back into the defensive line.
Defenders standing right next to the ruck to stop pick and go.
Stay connected with your teammates on defense. Don't leave gaps.
Having more players than the other team in an area.
A planned restart: scrum or lineout.
8 forwards from each team bind and push to restart play after small mistakes like a knock-on.
Props and hooker (1, 2, 3).
Locks (4, 5).
Flankers and 8 (6, 7, 8).
Props, hooker, and locks (1 to 5).
How players hold onto each other in a scrum, ruck, or maul.
The ref's three calls to set up a scrum.
Restart after the ball goes out of bounds. Two lines of players, the hooker throws the ball in.
The player lifted to catch the throw.
Players who lift and hold up the jumper.
A jumper and their lifters working as a unit. [HANNAH: confirm our usage]
Fake lift to fool the other team about where the throw is going.
Ball carrier on their feet, held by an opponent, with at least one teammate bound on. The group drives forward together.
Pushing the maul forward.
A player breaking off the lineout or maul to run with the ball.
The 8 picking up the ball from the base of the scrum and running.
Drop kick from the middle of halfway to start each half and after scores.
Restart with a drop kick from the 22 when the attacking team kicks or carries the ball dead in your in-goal.
Restart from your own goal line in certain situations, like when the ball is held up in your in-goal.
A high kick from the 9, usually from a ruck or scrum.
A kick that rolls and bounces along the ground.
A very high kick so your team can chase and compete for it.
A kick aimed to go out of bounds to gain ground.
Throwing the ball in fast from touch without waiting for a lineout.
Taking a penalty by tapping the ball with your foot and running.
Kick at goal after a try. Worth 2.
Drop kick through the posts in open play. Worth 3.
Ref lets play continue after a foul if the non-offending team benefits. If no benefit, they go back to the foul.
Dropping or knocking the ball forward. Scrum to the other team.
Passing the ball forward. Scrum to the other team.
The ball carrier is in the in-goal but can't ground the ball.
The area behind the try line where you score.
The ball has gone beyond the dead ball line or out of the in-goal.
10 minutes off the field. Your team plays a player down.
Sent off for the rest of the match.
Sanction for a serious foul. Options include kick at goal, kick to touch, tap and go, or scrum.
Sanction for a smaller foul. Can't kick at goal.
Ref warnings. Do it immediately.
